records.literal_gloss: And he said, no, but I [am the] commander of [the] army of YHWH; now I have come. And fell Joshua to his face to [the] ground, and bowed down, and said to him, what [is] my lord speaking to his slave?

en.L: And he said, "No, but I [am the] commander of the army of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; now I have come." And Joshua fell on his face to the ground and bowed down, and he said to him, "What [is] my lord saying to his slave?"
en.B: "Neither," he answered. "I am the commander of the army of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and now I have come." Then Joshua threw himself down with his face to the ground and bowed low. He said to him, "What does my lord wish to say to his servant?"
en.R: "No," he said. "I am the commander of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s army. I have come now." Then Joshua bowed down low with his face to the ground. He said, "My lord, I am your servant. What do you want to tell me?"

sw.L: Akasema, "Hapana, bali mimi [ni] mkuu wa jeshi la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}; sasa nimekuja." Yoshua akaanguka kifudifudi hadi chini, akasujudu, akamwambia, "Bwana wangu anamwambia nini mtumwa wake?"
sw.B: Akajibu, "Hapana. Mimi ni mkuu wa jeshi la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, na sasa nimekuja." Ndipo Yoshua alijitupa chini kifudifudi, akasujudu. Akamwambia, "Bwana wangu anataka kumwambia nini mtumishi wake?"
sw.R: Akasema, "Hapana. Mimi ni mkuu wa jeshi la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Nimekuja sasa." Ndipo Yoshua aliinama mpaka uso wake ukagusa ardhi. Akasema, "Bwana wangu, mimi ni mtumishi wako. Unataka kuniambia nini?"

es.L: Y él dijo: «No, sino que yo [soy el] comandante del ejército {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}; ahora he venido». Y Josué cayó sobre su rostro en tierra y se postró, y le dijo: «¿Qué dice mi señor a su esclavo?».
es.B: «Ni lo uno ni lo otro —respondió—. Yo soy el comandante del ejército {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, y ahora he venido». Entonces Josué se echó rostro en tierra y se postró. Le dijo: «¿Qué quiere decirle mi señor a su siervo?».
es.R: «No», dijo él. «Soy el comandante del ejército {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. Acabo de llegar». Entonces Josué se inclinó hasta tocar el suelo con la cara. Le dijo: «Mi señor, yo soy tu siervo. ¿Qué quieres decirme?».

fr.L: Et il dit : « Non, mais moi, [je suis] le chef de l’armée {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ; maintenant je suis venu. » Et Josué tomba sur sa face contre terre et se prosterna, et il lui dit : « Que dit mon seigneur à son esclave ? »
fr.B: « Ni l’un ni l’autre, répondit-il. Je suis le chef de l’armée {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, et maintenant je suis venu. » Alors Josué se jeta face contre terre et se prosterna. Il lui dit : « Que veut dire mon seigneur à son serviteur ? »
fr.R: « Non, a-t-il dit. Je suis le chef de l’armée {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. Je suis venu maintenant. » Alors Josué s’est prosterné très bas, le visage contre terre. Il a dit : « Mon seigneur, je suis ton serviteur. Que veux-tu me dire ? »

vi.L: Và người nói: "Không, nhưng ta [là] tướng chỉ huy đạo quân của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}; bây giờ ta đã đến." Và Giô-suê sấp mặt xuống đất và lạy, và nói với người: "Chúa tôi nói gì với đầy tớ mình?"
vi.B: Người đáp: "Không phải vậy. Ta là tướng chỉ huy đạo quân của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, và bây giờ ta đã đến." Giô-suê liền sấp mặt xuống đất và cúi lạy. Ông thưa với người: "Chúa tôi muốn truyền gì cho đầy tớ mình?"
vi.R: Người ấy đáp: "Không. Ta là tướng chỉ huy đạo quân của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Bây giờ ta đã đến." Giô-suê liền cúi sấp mặt xuống đất. Ông thưa: "Thưa chúa tôi, tôi là đầy tớ của chúa tôi. Chúa tôi muốn bảo tôi điều gì?"

ko.L: 그러자 그가 말했다. "아니다. 나는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 군대 사령관이다. 이제 내가 왔다." 그러자 여호수아가 얼굴을 땅에 대고 엎드려 절하며 그에게 말했다. "내 주께서 그분의 종에게 무엇을 말씀하시렵니까?"
ko.B: 그가 대답했다. "어느 편도 아니다. 나는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 군대 사령관이다. 이제 내가 왔다." 그러자 여호수아가 얼굴을 땅에 대고 엎드려 절하며 그에게 말했다. "내 주께서 이 종에게 무슨 말씀을 하시렵니까?"
ko.R: 그가 말했다. "아니다. 나는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 군대 사령관이다. 이제 내가 왔다." 그러자 여호수아는 얼굴을 땅에 대고 엎드려 절했다. 그리고 말했다. "내 주여, 저는 당신의 종입니다. 저에게 무슨 말씀을 하시렵니까?"

pt.L: E ele disse: "Não, mas eu [sou] o comandante do exército {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}; agora vim." E Josué caiu com o rosto em terra, e se prostrou, e lhe disse: "Que diz o meu senhor ao seu escravo?"
pt.B: "Nenhum dos dois", respondeu ele. "Eu sou o comandante do exército {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, e agora cheguei." Então Josué se lançou com o rosto em terra e se prostrou. Ele lhe disse: "Que deseja o meu senhor dizer ao seu servo?"
pt.R: "Não", disse ele. "Eu sou o comandante do exército {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}. Agora eu vim." Então Josué se curvou até o chão, com o rosto em terra. Ele disse: "Meu senhor, eu sou o seu servo. O que o senhor quer me dizer?"

decisions.choice: No
decisions.reason: The standard Hebrew text reads "no". Some manuscripts and the old Greek and Syriac translations read a word that sounds the same and means "to him" ("and he said to him"). The text here follows "no": he is not on either side as Joshua means it, because he comes for the LORD. Reviewers should check the manuscript evidence.

decisions.choice: the commander of the army of the LORD: a heavenly leader sent by the LORD; whether he is the LORD himself is not said
alternatives: the LORD himself appearing as a man
a chief angel who leads the LORD's heavenly army
decisions.reason: "The army of the LORD" is most likely the host of heaven, the angels who serve him (1 Kings 22:19; Psalm 103:20-21), though Israel's own tribes are once called "the armies of the LORD" (Exodus 12:41). The figure accepts Joshua's bowing and calls the ground holy (verse 15), as God does at the burning bush, where the angel of the LORD and God himself both speak (Exodus 3:2-6). In 6:2 the LORD speaks to Joshua, so the commander may be the LORD appearing in a man's form, as the angel of the LORD sometimes speaks as God (Genesis 16:7-13; 22:11-16; Numbers 22:22-35). But the text calls him only a man and a commander, Joshua addresses him as a man would a superior, and he may be an angel who comes with the LORD's authority. The passage leaves the question open.

decisions.choice: now I have come: his arrival is itself the message; what he came to say may follow in 6:2-5
alternatives: now I have come [to do something not stated]
decisions.reason: The words stand without a stated purpose. They may mean simply that he has now arrived to fight for Israel. The account may also break off here and continue in 6:2, where the LORD gives Joshua the plan for taking Jericho, with 6:1 as an aside.

decisions.choice: fell on his face and bowed down ... my lord ... his servant: the honor paid to a superior
decisions.reason: To fall face down and call oneself someone's servant is how a person shows deep respect, to a king or a heavenly visitor as well as to God (Genesis 18:2-3; 1 Samuel 25:23-24). The word for "my lord" here is the form used for a human master or a messenger, not the title reserved for God, so Joshua's words do not by themselves settle who the commander is.

decisions.choice: my lord (small l); slave at Literal, servant at Balanced and Readable; no capitalized pronouns for the commander
decisions.reason: Joshua uses the ordinary polite form of address, so "lord" is not capitalized, and because the text does not say plainly that the commander is God, the pronouns for him are not treated as pronouns for God (compare the angel of the LORD in Numbers 22). "Slave" and "servant" follow the project's usual rule for this word.

decisions.choice: "Bwana wangu" with a capital only because it begins the question; "mtumwa" (L), "mtumishi" (B, R); no deity_pronoun spans for the commander
alternatives: "bwana wangu" in lowercase within a sentence
decisions.reason: Joshua uses the ordinary polite address to a superior. Swahili "bwana" serves both as "sir" and "Lord", so the capital here comes only from its place at the start of Joshua's words; the text does not say whether the commander is the LORD himself, and the Swahili, like the English, gives him no capitalised pronouns.

decisions.choice: "mi señor" (small s), "tú"; "esclavo" (Literal), "siervo" (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Joshua uses the ordinary polite address, so "señor" is not capitalized and the commander's pronouns take no deity setting, as in the English. A single person is addressed with "tú" in this translation, so Readable says "tu siervo" and "¿Qué quieres decirme?".

decisions.choice: "chúa tôi" ... "đầy tớ mình" for Joshua's words; the commander says "ta"; no "Ngài"
decisions.reason: Joshua honors the commander as a superior: "chúa tôi" (my lord), the form the Genesis terms note gives for "my lord" spoken to someone other than God, in small letters, as the English keeps "my lord" with no capital. Whether the commander is the LORD himself is left open (m2), so Vietnamese does not use the "Ngài" it keeps for God, nor a capital "Ta" for his words. "đầy tớ" is used at every level, as for Moses in 1:1.

decisions.choice: "tướng chỉ huy đạo quân của CHÚA"
decisions.reason: The word for a military commander, with "đạo quân" (army, host) for the LORD's army.

decisions.choice: the commander speaks to Joshua in the plain style; Joshua answers in the formal polite style, with "내 주" and "종" ("저" at Readable)
alternatives: "주님", the word kept for God as Lord
decisions.reason: Joshua honors the commander as a superior, the way a servant speaks to a master. "내 주" is the form the terms of this translation give for "my lord" said to someone other than God; "주님" is not used, because the text does not say whether he is the LORD himself.

decisions.choice: o comandante do exército do SENHOR (every level)
alternatives: o príncipe do exército do SENHOR
o chefe do exército do SENHOR
decisions.reason: For the whole book. The title names a heavenly leader sent by the LORD (m2); "comandante" says plainly what the English "commander" says, where the older "príncipe" now suggests royalty. Readable keeps the same words, with the article inside the setting span: "do exército {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}".

decisions.choice: você (Joshua to the stranger, 5:13); meu senhor, o seu escravo (L) / servo (B, R), o senhor (Joshua bowing); tu (the commander to Joshua, 5:15)
decisions.reason: Joshua first takes the figure for a man (m2 of verse 13) and speaks to him with "você". Once he knows who he is, he bows and uses the courtly third person, "o meu senhor ... ao seu servo", and Readable "o senhor", as people speak to a superior (docs/pentateuch-portuguese-terms.md); "senhor" stays lowercase, since the text does not say that the commander is God (r-en-1). The commander answers with "tu", as the angels of Genesis 19 and Numbers 22 speak in Portuguese and as God speaks to Moses at the bush (Exodus 3:5).

source.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ שַׂר־צְבָ֨א יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־יְהוֹשֻׁ֗עַ שַׁל־נַֽעַלְךָ֙ מֵעַ֣ל רַגְלֶ֔ךָ כִּ֣י הַמָּק֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַתָּ֛ה עֹמֵ֥ד עָלָ֖יו קֹ֣דֶשׁ ה֑וּא וַיַּ֥עַשׂ יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ כֵּֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And said [the] commander of [the] army of YHWH to Joshua, take off your sandal from on your foot, for the place that you [are] standing on it, holy [is] it. And did Joshua so.

en.L: And the commander of the army of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Joshua, "Take off your sandal from your foot, for the place on which you [are] standing, it [is] holy." And Joshua did so.
en.B: The commander of the army of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Joshua, "Take the sandals off your feet. The place you are standing on is holy." And Joshua did so.
en.R: The commander of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s army told Joshua, "Take off your sandals. You are standing in a holy place." And Joshua did what he said.

sw.L: Mkuu wa jeshi la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia Yoshua, "Vua kiatu chako mguuni mwako, kwa maana mahali hapo unaposimama ni patakatifu." Yoshua akafanya hivyo.
sw.B: Mkuu wa jeshi la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimwambia Yoshua, "Vua viatu miguuni mwako, kwa sababu mahali unaposimama ni patakatifu." Naye Yoshua akafanya hivyo.
sw.R: Mkuu wa jeshi la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimwambia Yoshua, "Vua viatu vyako. Umesimama mahali patakatifu." Naye Yoshua akafanya kama alivyoambiwa.

es.L: Y el comandante del ejército {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} dijo a Josué: «Quítate la sandalia de tu pie, porque el lugar sobre el cual estás, santo [es]». Y Josué lo hizo así.
es.B: El comandante del ejército {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} le dijo a Josué: «Quítate las sandalias de los pies. El lugar donde estás es santo». Y Josué lo hizo así.
es.R: El comandante del ejército {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} le dijo a Josué: «Quítate las sandalias. Estás en un lugar santo». Y Josué hizo lo que él le dijo.

fr.L: Et le chef de l’armée {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} dit à Josué : « Ôte ta sandale de ton pied, car le lieu sur lequel tu te tiens, il [est] saint. » Et Josué fit ainsi.
fr.B: Le chef de l’armée {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} dit à Josué : « Retire les sandales de tes pieds. Le lieu où tu te tiens est saint. » Et Josué obéit.
fr.R: Le chef de l’armée {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} a dit à Josué : « Enlève tes sandales. Tu te tiens dans un lieu saint. » Et Josué a fait ce qu’il disait.

vi.L: Và tướng chỉ huy đạo quân của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} nói với Giô-suê: "Hãy cởi dép khỏi chân ngươi, vì nơi ngươi đang đứng, nơi ấy [là] thánh." Và Giô-suê làm như vậy.
vi.B: Tướng chỉ huy đạo quân của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} bảo Giô-suê: "Hãy cởi dép khỏi chân ông, vì nơi ông đang đứng là đất thánh." Và Giô-suê làm theo.
vi.R: Tướng chỉ huy đạo quân của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} bảo Giô-suê: "Hãy cởi dép ra. Ông đang đứng ở một nơi thánh." Và Giô-suê làm theo lời người.

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 군대 사령관이 여호수아에게 말했다. "네 발에서 네 신을 벗어라. 네가 서 있는 곳, 그곳은 거룩하다." 그러자 여호수아가 그렇게 했다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 군대 사령관이 여호수아에게 말했다. "네 발에서 신을 벗어라. 네가 서 있는 곳은 거룩한 곳이다." 여호수아는 그대로 했다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 군대 사령관이 여호수아에게 말했다. "신을 벗어라. 너는 거룩한 곳에 서 있다." 여호수아는 그가 말한 대로 했다.

pt.L: E o comandante do exército {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} disse a Josué: "Tira a tua sandália do teu pé, porque o lugar em que estás, ele [é] santo." E Josué fez assim.
pt.B: O comandante do exército {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} disse a Josué: "Tira as sandálias dos pés. O lugar onde estás é santo." E Josué assim fez.
pt.R: O comandante do exército {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} disse a Josué: "Tira as sandálias. Estás num lugar santo." E Josué fez o que ele disse.

decisions.choice: take off your sandal ... the place ... is holy: the words spoken to Moses at the burning bush
decisions.reason: The command is almost the same as Exodus 3:5. As the LORD met Moses before he led Israel out of Egypt, so Joshua is met before he leads Israel into the land (compare 1:5; 3:7). The place is holy because the LORD's presence is there, not because of anything in the ground itself.

decisions.choice: your sandal ... your foot: a singular meant as a whole
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has the singular, where Exodus 3:5 has the plural. The singular stands for both; Joshua is to go barefoot.

decisions.choice: Joshua did so: the scene ends with his obedience
decisions.reason: No further words are reported here. The next verses describe Jericho shut tight (6:1), and the LORD then speaks to Joshua (6:2), so the commander's coming leads into the taking of the city.

decisions.choice: sandals ... feet
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the plural, which is what the singular means here (m2).
